page_title: Making your own Face Recognition System

sources.entry: Make your Own Face Recognition System

summary.title: Making your own Face Recognition System
summary.one_liner: You learn how FaceNet's triplet loss and Siamese architecture work, and how to build a simple Python/Keras face recognition system that matches webcam faces against a database of one image per person.
takeaways: FaceNet maps face images to a 128-number Euclidean embedding where smaller distance means more similar faces.
Triplet loss pulls an anchor toward a positive (same identity) and pushes it away from a negative (different identity), with margin alpha.
A Siamese network shares identical weights across inputs so their outputs can be compared by distance.
Recognition is done by encoding a new face, finding the closest database encoding, and rejecting matches above a threshold (0.52 in the author's trial-and-error setup).
summary.summary: The article explains the background of FaceNet, covering its triplet loss function and Siamese network design, then walks through an implementation in Python using Keras and TensorFlow. It loads a pre-trained FaceNet model with utility files from deeplearning.ai, defines the triplet loss, and compiles the model with Adam. It then builds a database from one image per person, identifies a new face by nearest encoding distance, and applies a threshold to reject unknown faces. A webcam demo from the linked GitHub repository is mentioned, but the article focuses on the core code.
